newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker, underperform U.S. curve.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker, underperform U.S. curve.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Thursday, underperforming U.S. issues, as a drop in the Canadian dollar and profit taking after gains on Wednesday weighed on prices, analysts said.

"It's just a little rebalancing of what had happened yesterday. Yesterday we outperformed the U.S. with particular interest in the two and five-year area," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed income with Altamira Investment. "We're going back to Tuesday's Canada-U.S. spread levels."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond softened to yield C$0.10 to C$108.10 to yield 7.30 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 7.08 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 22 basis points from 20 basis points on Wednesday.
"The Canadian marketplace was caught without bonds yesterday and it drove prices up," said Sutherland.

Weighing on the Canadian market this morning was a softer Canadian dollar. Canada's dollar opened weaker in heavy trading at C$1.3992 (US$0.7146) after reaching a two-year low of C$1.4018 (US$0.7133) in overnight trade. The unit weakened from the open after the release of the Canadian merchandise trade surplus for February.
The merchandise trade surplus widened in February to C$2.19 million. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.35 billion in February.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada will release details of it upcoming 30-year bond auction at 1530 EDT/1930 GMT. The auction will take place April 23 and will be dated and delivered May 1.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$101.75 to yield 6.748 percent. The U.S. bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 14 basis points on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.18 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.30 percent.
